name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Saturday 4 January 1975

clue.text: Leader of the windbags?

blocks.note: surface reading: the chief of a crowd of tiresome talkers
setter's reading: bagpipes, instruments that are literally bags of wind, and the man who leads a pipe band

explanation.surface: A jibe at whoever heads a group of long-winded bores.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is PIPE MAJOR, the head of a military pipe band; the bagpipes are the 'windbags' he leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe major is the senior piper who directs a band of bagpipers.

clue.text: Choose to express gratitude to an old sycophant

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
to thank is to express gratitude

explanation.surface: Deciding to show appreciation to an elderly flatterer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the answer as archaic: a pickthank was a flatterer who curried favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickthank is an obsolete word for a toady or flatterer seeking favour.

clue.text: Interval for father to employ

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to use something is to employ it

explanation.surface: A break in work for Dad to take on staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short break or interval in activity.

clue.text: Much slaughter in the service area

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: Heavy killing in a military zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service area' looks like one military or motorway phrase; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the brutal killing of many people at once.

clue.text: Is it rigged up for trial purposes?

definitions.text: Is it rigged up for trial purposes?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fixed court case
setter's reading: a makeshift ship's mast put up in an emergency, with a jury being the body at a trial

explanation.surface: Asks whether a court case has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Jury-rigged means improvised; a jury-mast is a temporary mast rigged after the original is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury-mast is a temporary mast rigged on a ship to replace a broken one.

clue.text: She has a tiff with another girl

blocks.note: a row is a quarrel or tiff
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl falling out with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: the answer is simply a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a woman's name, and 'she' stands for any female person.

clue.text: His BA could make a gentleman of him

definitions.text: His BA could make a gentleman of him

indicators.note: to make something from letters is to rework them into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university degree might turn a man into a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: rearranging the letters of 'His BA' produces SAHIB, a title for a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the respectful Indian form of address for a European man, effectively 'sir' or gentleman.

clue.text: Fool of a woman

blocks.note: surface reading: a silly woman
setter's reading: the beast whose name means a fool, here a female one

explanation.walkthrough: An ass is both a fool and a donkey; a she-ass is a female donkey, so the clue reads as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-ass is a female donkey, and ass is a standard word for a fool.

clue.text: They succeed even in a man's world

definitions.text: They succeed even in a man's world

blocks.clueFragment: They succeed even in a man's world
blocks.note: surface reading: women who do well in male-dominated careers
setter's reading: women who inherit, succeeding to an estate

explanation.surface: A tribute to women who prosper despite male dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: Heiresses are women who inherit property, so they succeed to it.

clue.text: Outstandingly masterful?

blocks.note: surface reading: brilliantly skilled
setter's reading: covered in bosses, studs that stand out from a surface; and domineering

explanation.walkthrough: A boss is a raised knob or stud, so a surface with bosses is literally outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossy means domineering, inclined to order others about like a master.

clue.text: Just the one to run through a menu?

definitions.text: Just the one to run through a menu?

blocks.clueFragment: Just the one to run through a menu?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone ideal for reading a restaurant's list of dishes
setter's reading: a swift runner, a horse bred for racing, punning on the courses of a meal

explanation.surface: A diner keen enough to work through every dish on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A COURSER is a fast horse; a menu is made of courses, so the runner is the natural one to go through them.
explanation.definitionFit: A courser is a poetic word for a swift horse, an animal made for running.

clue.text: We are up against calamities with these pests

indicators.note: being up against something means standing right next to it, so the two parts sit side by side

blocks.note: taken as written
evils are misfortunes or disasters

explanation.surface: A farmer lamenting a plague of pests among other troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils are small beetles that infest grain and other stored food, a classic pest.

clue.text: Letter shows the task is half-completed

indicators.note: only half of the word is finished, so the rest of it is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before it is cut in half

explanation.surface: A note reporting that a job is only half done.
explanation.walkthrough: THE stays whole and only the first half of TASK, TA, survives, giving THETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Music by The Brothers in this garden?

definitions.text: Music by The Brothers in this garden?

blocks.note: surface reading: songs by a family pop group
setter's reading: the brothers are monks, and the music is a well-known light orchestral piece by Albert Ketelbey named after their garden

explanation.surface: Asks where a band of brothers might be heard playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a Monastery Garden' is a popular 1915 orchestral piece by Albert Ketelbey; monks are called Brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the home of a community of monks, who address each other as brother.

clue.text: He makes a beeline for his work

definitions.text: He makes a beeline for his work

blocks.clueFragment: makes a beeline for his work
blocks.note: surface reading: a keen employee who heads straight to his job
setter's reading: his line of work is bees

explanation.surface: An eager worker hurrying straight to the office each morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiarist is a beekeeper, someone whose occupation is tending hives.

clue.text: Suggests a matter of duty to a clergyman

blocks.note: first meaning: obligatory, as in 'it is ___ on you'
second meaning: the holder of a parish living

explanation.surface: Hinting to a vicar that something is his obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used as an adjective for a duty and as a noun for the priest of a parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Incumbent means obligatory, and an incumbent is the clergyman holding a benefice.

clue.text: The Thames, in part, is taking one south

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A geographical note about a stretch of the Thames heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name given to the Thames as it flows through Oxford, hence only part of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis is the local name for the upper stretch of the river Thames around Oxford.

clue.text: Their products are good for a season at least

definitions.text: Their products are good for a season at least

blocks.clueFragment: good for a season at least
blocks.note: surface reading: goods that last at least one season, like fashions
setter's reading: to season food, which their product is good for

explanation.surface: Praise for durable goods that last a season or more.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt mines produce rock salt, which is used for seasoning food.

clue.text: Confections — for keeping washer-women's hair in order?

definitions.text: Confections — for keeping washer-women's hair in order?

blocks.note: surface reading: sweet baked goods

blocks.clueFragment: for keeping washer-women's hair in order
blocks.note: setter's reading: a tub for washing plus the knots of hair women pin up

explanation.surface: Sweets offered alongside a tip for laundresses' hairstyles.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bath bun is a sweet currant bun from the city of Bath; a bun is also hair coiled at the back of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath buns are rich sugar-topped yeast buns, a kind of confection.

clue.text: Rose for the meat

blocks.note: first meaning: a class of climbing garden rose
second meaning: a small round boneless cut, usually of lamb

explanation.surface: A rose garnishing a plate of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisette names both a type of rose bred in America and a small round fillet of lamb.

clue.text: Punters do this as well as place bets

definitions.text: Punters do this as well as place bets

blocks.note: surface reading: gamblers, who place bets

blocks.clueFragment: Punters do this as well as place
blocks.note: setter's reading: footballers who punt the ball, and those taking a place-shot from the ground, both strike it with the boot

explanation.surface: Gamblers at the races laying their money down.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and American football a punt is a kick dropped from the hands, and a place kick is taken from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick is to strike with the foot, which is what both a punt and a place kick involve.

clue.text: Pleasurable means of going around in the States

definitions.text: Pleasurable means of going around in the States

blocks.note: surface reading: an enjoyable way to tour America
setter's reading: literally turning round and round, on the fairground ride Americans call by this name

explanation.surface: Recommends a fun way of travelling across America.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say carousel where the British say merry-go-round or roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is the American term for a merry-go-round, a fairground ride that revolves for fun.

clue.text: Proverbially a capital place for a tug-of-war

definitions.text: Proverbially a capital place for a tug-of-war

blocks.clueFragment: a capital place for a tug-of-war
blocks.note: surface reading: an excellent venue for a rope-pulling contest
setter's reading: the saying 'When Greek meets Greek, then comes the tug of war', with capital meaning a national seat of government

explanation.surface: Recommends a fine spot to hold a rope-pulling match.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, home of the Greeks in the proverb about a tug of war.

clue.text: How can you make a cat sit still?

indicators.note: asking how to make something invites building it out of the parts on offer in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat owner's despairing question about a restless pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb ending the question, but it is the definition, meaning motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving or at rest, as something still is.

clue.text: Painful outcome of running along the Border?

definitions.text: Painful outcome of running along the Border?

blocks.note: surface reading: the sharp side pain a runner gets
setter's reading: needlework, a running stitch worked along the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: A jogger along the Scottish Border gets a pain in the side.
explanation.walkthrough: A stitch is the pain from running; a hem is a border of fabric, and hemstitch is a decorative stitch sewn along it. The capital B hints at the England-Scotland Border.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemstitch is an ornamental sewing stitch used to finish the hem, or edge, of a piece of fabric.

clue.text: A flighty person might take to them

definitions.text: A flighty person might take to them

blocks.note: surface reading: a fickle, capricious type

blocks.clueFragment: A flighty person might take to them
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone given to flight runs off, in the idiom 'take to one's ___'

explanation.surface: Something a fickle person might suddenly become fond of.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to one's heels is an idiom meaning to run away, as someone fleeing would.

clue.text: Churchill related its gathering

blocks.note: surface reading: the wartime leader reported on some assembly
setter's reading: the title of the first volume of Churchill's history of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Churchill giving an account of a meeting he attended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Gathering Storm' (1948) is the first volume of Churchill's 'The Second World War'.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is the thing that gathers in the title of Churchill's book about the approach of war.

clue.text: Some took a picture of an animal

indicators.note: 'some' asks for just a portion of the following words, read straight through

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: A photographer snapping wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a central African mammal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Scene of large-scale operations

blocks.note: surface reading: big military or business campaigns
setter's reading: to scale is to climb, and here is the largest thing on earth to climb

explanation.surface: Describes the theatre of a major military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, the scene of famous climbing expeditions.

clue.text: At any rate it won't run people down

definitions.text: At any rate it won't run people down

blocks.note: surface reading: a vehicle that will never knock anyone over, whatever its speed
setter's reading: carry passengers down the line, away from the capital, which this service never does

explanation.surface: Reassurance that some vehicle is safe at any speed.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways 'up' trains run towards London and 'down' trains away from it, so whatever its speed this train only carries people up.
explanation.definitionFit: An up train is a railway service travelling towards the main terminus, the opposite of a down train.

clue.text: What makes one fed up might be an asset

indicators.note: 'might be' offers what the word could turn into if its letters were rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry thought that whatever bores you could still be worth something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' here means fully fed, not bored.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate someone is to satisfy their appetite completely, filling them with food.

clue.text: They're prepared to be bought at their face value.

definitions.text: They're prepared to be bought at their face value.

blocks.note: surface reading: goods sold for the price printed on them
setter's reading: prepared products bought for what they do for the face

explanation.surface: Stamps or banknotes offered at exactly the printed price.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetics are preparations such as powder and lipstick applied to improve the face.
